info.title: pforte admin API
info.description: Manage users, claims, clients and the audit log of a pforte identity service. Authenticate with an access token from the OAuth `client_credentials` grant of a client registered with the scope `admin` (everything) or `directory` (users and claims only). Errors are RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` documents.

bearerAuth.description: Access token from the client_credentials grant (POST /token) of an admin client.

get.description: The caller of this request: a machine (a client with its scopes) or a person signed in to the administration UI.
Newest last. Pass `nextCursor` as `cursor` to get the following page.

patch.description: Only the fields given are changed. Nothing is written when nothing differs.

delete.description: Removes the user, their claims and devices. The audit log keeps who they were.

put.summary: Create or update a user by e-mail
put.description:
Idempotent, so an hourly import can call it blindly. Updates names, phone and language; never the password, status or administrator rights. With `claims`, replaces the values of exactly the claim types given (see PUT /users/{id}/claims). Writes nothing and says `unchanged` when nothing differs. Everything happens in one transaction: if a claim is invalid, the user is not created or changed either.

With `dryRun=true` the same checks and the same diff run, then everything is rolled back: nothing is written and no audit event is recorded. The answer says what would happen (`created`, `updated`, `unchanged`) and what would change, so a dry run cannot disagree with the real call.

get.summary: The claim values of a user

put.description: Replaces the values of exactly the claim types given and leaves every other claim of the user untouched. An empty list removes all values of a type. All values are checked first; if any is invalid nothing is changed.

put.summary: Set the values of one claim type

post.summary: Add one value to a claim type
post.description: Does nothing if the user already has the value. A single-valued type refuses a second, different value.

delete.summary: Remove one value of a claim type
delete.description: Does nothing if the user does not have the value.

get.summary: List the remembered devices of a user
get.description: Devices that skip the second factor: not revoked and not expired. Most recently seen first.

delete.summary: Revoke all remembered devices of a user
delete.description: Every sign-in of the user asks for the code again. Locking, deactivating, resetting the password and ending sessions do this as well.
The next sign-in on that device asks for the code again.

get.summary: Where a user is signed in
get.description: The browser sessions (single sign-on) that are open, and the applications that were granted access and stay signed in, such as an app on a phone. Identifiers and tokens are not returned. `POST /users/{id}/end-sessions` ends them all.

post.description: For a created or active user. Ends all their sessions and refresh tokens; they cannot sign in until unlocked.

For a locked user: they become active again, or created if they never set a password. For an active user, who is not locked, nothing changes except that the failed sign-in attempts held against their address are forgotten, so they can try again at once after too many mistakes.
For someone who has left. Ends all sessions and refresh tokens and cancels a pending activation link.

For a created user: sends the activation link, where they choose their first password; a new call replaces the earlier link. For a deactivated user who already has a password: makes them active again, without a link. The link is never returned or logged by pforte. The body is optional; with `clientId` (a registered client) the e-mail names the application and the page after choosing the password leads to its start address (`clientUri`); an unknown client is a 400.

post.summary: Reset the password of a user
post.description: For an active user. Sends them a code to choose a new password and ends all their sessions and refresh tokens, since the account may be compromised.

post.summary: End all sessions of a user
post.description: Deletes their sessions, grants and refresh tokens and revokes their remembered devices, so they must sign in again, with a code. Their status does not change.
The key is the claim name in tokens. Names that tokens already use (email, name, …) are reserved.

patch.description: Refused with 409 when existing values would violate the change: a new pattern they do not match, or single-valued while a user holds several values.

delete.description: Refused with 409 while users hold values of it. With `force=true` the values are deleted too, and the audit log records how many users and values were affected.

get.summary: The claim types a client receives

put.summary: Set the claim types a client receives
put.description: Replaces the whole set. A client only ever receives the claim types assigned to it.

post.description: Two kinds exist. An **application** signs users in (authorization code flow, public or confidential) and has OpenID scopes and redirect URIs. A **machine** calls the admin API with the client_credentials grant and has only the scopes `admin` and/or `directory`. They never mix. A confidential client gets a generated secret, returned here once and never again. Redirect URIs and the start address (`clientUri`) must be https (http only for localhost).

patch.description: Only the fields given are changed, and the result must still be a valid client of its kind. Takes effect at once. The last client with the `admin` scope cannot lose it.

delete.description: Also removes its claim type assignments and revokes every grant and token issued to it. Refused for the last client with the `admin` scope and for the client making the call.

post.summary: Replace the secret of a confidential client
post.description: The old secret stops working at once. The new one is returned here once and never again.

get.description: Newest first. Every change through the admin API and every lifecycle action is recorded with the client that made it. Pass `nextCursor` as `cursor` to get older events; the order is stable while new events arrive.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: An exact action such as `user.lock`, or a prefix ending in `*` such as `user.*`.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Only events at or after this time (ISO 8601).
